chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Al-A'ala ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)

Regarding the woman from whom the blood of menstruation ceases at the end of her days, he (peace be upon him) said: When her husband is seized by craving, let him instruct her to wash her private part, then he may touch her, if he wishes, before she performs the full ritual bath.
ai.seo_question: What purification is required for a woman whose period ends at the last day before marital intimacy?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the distinction between the cessation of bleeding and the obligation of full ritual bath (ghusl), permitting sexual intimacy once the woman performs local cleansing (istinja) if her husband desires, even before completing the full ghusl. It reflects the Shia juristic view that the prohibition of intercourse during menstruation is lifted immediately upon the cessation of blood, provided the woman is clean, highlighting a nuanced approach to purity laws in marital relations.
